# discuss

> Launch a live browser review session for a Markdown file.
> Discuss renders the document locally, serves a loopback web UI, and records threaded comments, replies, takes, resolutions, and a final transcript.

## Install

Pre-built binary:
  curl -sSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisraethke/discuss-cli/main/install.sh | sh

From a clone (requires Rust):
  git clone https://github.com/chrisraethke/discuss-cli.git
  cd discuss-cli
  sh install.sh

## Quick Start

Review a Markdown file:
  discuss path/to/review.md

Review a running website through a fixed-upstream second loopback origin:
  discuss http://localhost:3000
  discuss https://example.test/path

Review a GitHub PR privately (full URL only; requires an active authenticated-gh agent):
  discuss pr https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/NUMBER

Pin the port and suppress browser auto-open:
  discuss --port 9000 --no-open path/to/review.md

When discuss starts it binds `127.0.0.1` and prints the actual address:
  review UI/API: http://127.0.0.1:<port>

Without a CLI, environment, or TOML port override, discuss binds port 0 directly
and uses the OS-assigned port. It does not scan for a free-looking port first.
An explicit nonzero port binds exactly and exits 3 if occupied; it never falls
back. Open the reported URL in a browser. When the review is complete, click
Finish review to finish the session.

## CLI

Main command:
  discuss [--port N] [--no-open] [--no-save] [--history-dir PATH] [--verdict-options SPEC] [--verdict-prompt TEXT] FILE|HTTP(S)_URL

Private-first PR command:
  discuss [--port N] [--no-open] [--no-save] [--history-dir PATH] pr https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/NUMBER

Update check:
  discuss update --check

Flags:
  --port N            Bind this exact nonzero port; when omitted, the OS assigns a port.
  --no-open           Do not open the browser automatically after the server starts.
  --no-save           Do not write a history archive when the review is done.
  --history-dir PATH  Write history archives under this directory for this invocation.
  --verdict-options SPEC  Offer finish-review choices; grammar is id[:label][:style][!] separated by |. Use single quotes because | is a pipe and ! can trigger history expansion, e.g. 'approved:Approve|declined:Decline:negative!'. Must precede diff.
  --verdict-prompt TEXT   Custom prompt above verdict options; without --verdict-options it warns on stderr.

`discuss update --check` checks GitHub Releases for a newer version. Discuss never checks automatically.

## Configuration

Config sources are applied in this order, with later sources winning:
  ~/.discuss/discuss.config.toml
  ./discuss.config.toml
  DISCUSS_* environment variables
  CLI flags

Supported settings:
  port = 7777                         # optional explicit pin; omit for OS assignment
  auto_open = true
  idle_timeout_secs = 600
  history_dir = "/path/to/history"   # optional; default is ~/.discuss/history
  no_save = false
  log_level = "info"                 # optional; DISCUSS_LOG overrides it

Environment variables:
  DISCUSS_PORT
  DISCUSS_AUTO_OPEN
  DISCUSS_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS
  DISCUSS_HISTORY_DIR
  DISCUSS_NO_SAVE
  DISCUSS_LOG

Example `discuss.config.toml` with an explicitly pinned port:
  port = 7777
  auto_open = true
  idle_timeout_secs = 600
  history_dir = "/Users/alice/.discuss/history"
  no_save = false
  log_level = "info"

## Runtime Model

- `stdout` is reserved for JSONL events.
- `stderr` is reserved for status and error text.
- The first stdout event for a normal session is `session.started`. Existing payload fields are preserved; `apiBaseUrl`, `endpoints` (`state`, `events`, `createThread`, `addTakeTemplate` with literal `{threadId}`, `blocksTemplate` with literal `{fileId}`, `done`), and short `agentInstructions` (including the invitation to pre-annotate edited documents with `kind: "agent"` threads) are additive. Agents must retain and use those exact endpoint URLs.
- A sole HTTP/S argument starts live mode. `session.started` includes `mode: "live"`, `upstreamUrl`, and `proxyUrl`. The proxy is a fixed-upstream loopback website origin, never a Discuss API origin; agents must not send REST mutations to it. With no explicit port, both listener ports are OS-assigned. With `--port N`, the API binds N and the proxy binds N+1, failing before readiness if either is occupied.
- Live HTML is inspector-injected and route-scoped; `elementAnchor` includes `route`, `selector`, optional `accessibleName`, and `outerHtml`. Authentication is limited: upstream browser cookies do not implicitly belong to the proxy origin, and v1 provides no cookie import flags or production-site compatibility guarantee.
- PR mode accepts only a strict full github.com PR URL and rejects positional files and verdict flags. It requires an installed, authenticated `gh` CLI; missing `gh` fails before readiness with platform installation and `gh auth login` instructions. Discuss shells directly to read-only `gh`/`git` commands without receiving or storing a token, loads metadata/discussion concurrently, uses an authenticated temporary filtered clone, and generates exactly one aggregate git diff with `--unified=<N>` (10 by default, overridden by the PR subcommand's `--unified <N>`). The resulting overview plus one diff file per changed path are imported automatically. `session.started` reports `prImportMode: "automatic"`; the agent waits for `pr.imported` and remains responsible only for requested AI summaries and explicitly confirmed publication.
- PR questions and answers stay local. Finish review uses explicit include controls (off by default), an editable AI summary, and a text-first exact GFM confirmation. Only the resulting `pr.publish.requested` event authorizes the agent to publish. New inline comments are grouped in one review; only confidently resolved existing review threads receive replies. Failures preserve edits; success emits `session.done`. Standalone PR comments are out of scope.
- When the review finishes, discuss emits `session.done` with the final transcript payload. With `--verdict-options`, finishing requires the human to pick a verdict, which is included in that payload.
- After `idle_timeout_secs` of inactivity, discuss emits `prompt.suggest_done`. Set `idle_timeout_secs = 0` to disable that prompt.
- Logs are written under `~/.discuss/logs`.

Event kinds:
  session.started
  thread.created
  thread.deleted
  thread.resolved
  thread.unresolved
  reply.added
  take.added
  draft.updated
  draft.cleared
  prompt.suggest_done
  pr.imported
  pr.summary.requested
  pr.publish.requested
  session.done

## History Archives

Unless `--no-save` or `no_save = true` is set, discuss writes the final transcript JSON to:
  <history_dir>/<sanitized source stem>/<completed-at>.json

Example:
  ~/.discuss/history/review_plan/2026-04-23T02:30:00Z.json

The `session.done` payload and the saved archive use the same transcript shape; when verdict options are used it may include an optional verdict object:
  {
    "threads": [
      {
        "id": "u-1",
        "anchorStart": 2,
        "anchorEnd": 3,
        "snippet": "snippet u-1",
        "breadcrumb": "Overview > Goals",
        "text": "initial comment u-1",
        "kind": "user",
        "replies": [],
        "takes": [],
        "resolution": null,
        "createdAt": "2026-04-23T02:30:02Z",
        "deletedAt": null
      }
    ],
    "verdict": {
      "optionId": "declined",
      "label": "Decline",
      "feedback": "needs a migration plan for step 3",
      "decidedAt": "2026-04-23T02:30:20Z"
    }
  }

`kind` may also be "agent" (an agent-created annotation whose opening prose is stored as the thread's first take).

## Exit Codes

  0  Clean exit (Done, or update completed)
  1  Generic failure (file not found, render error, logging error, update error)
  2  Configuration / parse error
  3  Port already in use (or other server bind failure)
  5  Interrupted (Ctrl+C)
